Date: 2023-03-08
Remarks
Reconsideration is requested in view of the above amendments and the following remarks. The amendments to claim 9 are supported by the original disclosure, for example paragraph [0044]. No new matter has been added. Claims 1-29 are pending.
Claims 9-16 are objected to for the reasons noted. Applicant disagrees with the objection. Breadth of claim language should not be confused with clarity. This is exactly what the objection is doing by stating that what the adjustment is relative to "is unclear". If the claim language is unclear, the claim should be rejected under 35 USC 112.
Nonetheless, claim 9 has been amended to recite that the adjustment is relative to a housing of the non-invasive analyte sensor.
Claims 9-13 are rejected under 35 USC 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by US 2019/0008422 to Leath.
In addition, claims 1-5, 17-20, 23-24, and 27-28 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over Leath in view of Lucyszyn.
In addition, claims 6-7, 21-22 and 25-26 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over Leath and Lucyszyn, and further in view of US 2022/0413143 to Parsa.
In addition, claims 8 and 29 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over Leath and Lucyszyn, and in view of Ruiz.
In addition, claims 14-15 are rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over Leath in view of Parsa.
In addition, claim 16 is rejected under 35 USC 103 as being unpatentable over Leath in view of Ruiz.
With respect to claim 9, Leath does not teach or suggest at least one component associated with transmitting the transmit signal and/or associated with detecting the response signal is adjustable in position relative to a housing of the non-invasive analyte sensor between a first detecting position at which detection of the at least one analyte takes place and a second detecting position at which detection of the at least one analyte takes place. No components in Leath are adjustable relative to the housing. In addition, when the sensor is moved to different body parts, the housing and the components associated with transmitting the transmit signal and/or associated with detecting the response signal move with the housing. There is no movement relative to the housing.
Claims 10-16 depend from claim 9 and are patentable therewith for that reason alone and need not be separately distinguished at this time. Applicant does not concede the rejections to the dependent claims.
With respect to claims 1 and 17, Applicant submits that Leath and Lucyszyn are not properly combinable in the manner proposed. In particular, Lucyszyn is not analogous prior art to the claimed invention. A reference is analogous art to the claimed invention if: (1) the reference is from the same field of endeavor as the claimed invention (even if it addresses a different problem); or (2) the reference is reasonably pertinent to the problem faced by the inventor (even if it is not in the same field of endeavor as the claimed invention). MPEP 2141.01(a).
Lucyszyn is directed to an RF MEMS antenna for a generic transmit antenna application where the transmit antenna(s) physically move under some form of mechanical actuation mechanism. See page 1988, left column, Introduction, paragraph 3. There is no disclosure in Lucyszyn that the RF MEMS antenna can be used in a non- invasive analyte sensor. The claimed invention is directed to a non-invasive analyte sensor. Accordingly, Lucyszyn is not from the same field of endeavor as the claimed invention.
In addition, Lucyszyn is not reasonably pertinent to the problem faced by the inventor. The inventor was concerned with designing a non-invasive analyte sensor with or more adjustable transit and/or receive components whose physical position can be adjusted to permit adjustment of the sensing performance of the sensor. See paragraphs [0004] and [0037].
In Lucyszyn, although the RF MEMS antenna is adjustable, there is no disclosure that the RF MEMS antenna is suitable for use in a non-invasive analyte sensor, or that adjustment of the position of the RF MEMS antenna is for adjusting performance of such a sensor.
Since (1) Lucyszyn is not from the same field of endeavor as the claimed invention, and (2) Lucyszyn is not reasonably pertinent to the problem faced by the inventor, Lucyszyn is not analogous prior art that can be relied on under 35 U.S.C. 103.
Accordingly, Lucyszyn is not analogous prior art, and there is no suggestion or motivation to modify Leath with Lucyszyn.
For at least these reasons, claims 1 and 17 are patentable over Leath Lucyszyn. Claims 2-8 and 18-29 depend from claims 1 and 17, respectively, and are patentable therewith for that reason alone and need not be separately distinguished at this time. Applicant does not concede the rejections to the dependent claims.
With respect to the rejections relying upon Parsa, Applicant submits that a person of ordinary skill in the art would not modify Leath based on Parsa. Parsa teaches a sensing device to detect a biomarker, where the sensing device includes a mirror 10 that is adjustable in position to reflect a light beam over a range of angles. Paragraph [0162]; Figure 3D. However, due to the longer wavelength of a radio wave (used in Leath) compared to a light wave as taught by Parsa, the mirror of Parsa would not necessarily be suitable to achieve a reflection of the radio waves in Leath.
There is no teaching in Leath or Parsa as to how a mirror as taught by Parsa can be incorporated into Leath to achieve reflection of the radio waves used by Leath.
Favorable reconsideration in the form of a notice of allowance is requested. Any questions concerning this paper can be directed to the attention of the undersigned at (612) 455-3805.
Respectfully submitted,
SVG
